title: Which government will form after the 2026 New Zealand general election?
resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve according to the New Zealand government following the 2026 parliamentary elections based on the following criteria:

* **Labour-led**, if the government formed is led by the Labour Party irrespective of which other parties are in coalition.
* **National-led**, if the government formed is led by the National Party, irrespective of which other parties are in coalition.
* **Other**, if the government formed is led by a party other than the Labour or National Party.

If no government is formed before January 2027, this question will resolve as **None before January**.

The New Zealand Government will be the primary source for resolution, such as the seating plan for the 55th Parliament.
fine_print: Transitional/caretaker governments will not qualify for this question.

comments.author: Koboh
comments.text:
My prediction is a **narrow National led government, with around a 55% chance**. National and Labour are virtually tied in the latest polls, so I don’t think the party vote leader alone will determine the result. The real question is which side can assemble a workable parliamentary majority.

National’s path depends on ACT and New Zealand First, while Labour needs the Greens and potentially the Opportunity Party to translate their support into enough seats. TOP could be the biggest wild card if it clears the 5% threshold, the coalition arithmetic could shift significantly toward the centre left. I’m giving National a modest edge, not because the race is settled, but because coalition negotiations may be just as important as election night vote shares. This remains a close and highly uncertain contest.

**My final call:**

Select **National led**, at **55%**. The strongest reason to keep Labour led at 35% is that a small change in party support or the success of smaller parties could change which bloc reaches a majority.

comments.author: DaiLothbrook
comments.text:
>   I started from a slight historical edge for Labour-led government formation, but the newest seat projections make me lean National-led. Roy Morgan and Curia both project the current National–ACT–NZ First parties at or above a governing majority, although the latest RNZ and Verian polls disagree about which major party is ahead and suggest smaller parties could be pivotal.Fir the tine being, I am moving my central estimate to 56% National-led, not higher, I think  coalition arithmetic is too uncertain 

Sources: [Roy Morgan](https://www.roymorgan.com/findings/10351-nz-national-voting-intention-september-2026), [Curia poll](https://www.taxpayers.org.nz/oct2026_nztucurpolljjhhfas), [RNZ–Reid poll report](https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/06-10-2026/rnz-reid-research-poll-national-crashes-greens-surge-opportunity-kingmaker).
